question.worked_solution:
Notice that the logarithms share the same base.

First, we apply the power rule to the *first* term to make the coefficient in front of each logarithm the same:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{log}_{18}⁡(3x)+{log}_{18}⁡x & =1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡((3x)^{2})+{log}_{18}⁡x & =1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡(9{x}^{2})+{log}_{18}⁡x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we combine the logarithms using the product rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{18}⁡(9{x}^{2}\cdot x) & =1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡(9{x}^{3}) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing this equation in its equivalent exponential form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{18}^{{log}_{18}⁡(9{x}^{3})} & ={18}^{1} \\ 9{x}^{3} & =18\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve this quadratic equation for $x$ using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3} & =2 \\ x & =\sqrt[3]{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for an extraneous solution by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=\sqrt[3]{2}$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{log}_{18}⁡(3\cdot \sqrt[3]{2})+{log}_{18}⁡\sqrt[3]{2} & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡((3\sqrt[3]{2})^{2})+{log}_{18}⁡\sqrt[3]{2} & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡(({3}^{2}\sqrt[3]{{2}^{2}})+{log}_{18}⁡\sqrt[3]{2} & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡9\sqrt[3]{4}+{log}_{18}⁡\sqrt[3]{2} & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡(9\sqrt[3]{4}\cdot \sqrt[3]{2}) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡(9\cdot \sqrt[3]{8}) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡(9\cdot 2) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{18}⁡(18) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ 1 & =1.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=\sqrt[3]{2}$ is a valid solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$x=\sqrt[3]{2}$ only."
